origin.description: Read or replace the progression handlers, and record whether the global handler is enabled.
origin.usage: handlers(..., append = FALSE, on_missing = c("error", "warning", "ignore"), default = handler_txtprogressbar, global = NULL)

arguments.text: Handlers, or one list of handlers. A string looks up handler_<name> and then <name>.

arguments.name: append
arguments.text: If TRUE, concatenate onto the current list. The call returns the previous list.

arguments.name: on_missing
arguments.text: error, warning, or ignore when a named handler is missing. A unique prefix matches.

arguments.name: global
arguments.text: TRUE enables the global handler, FALSE disables it, and NA queries it.

origin.details: With no arguments, return the current list or the default. Setting returns the previous list. A validator that returns false drops that handler. The global flag is recorded without registering an RStudio or Shiny handler.
origin.value: The current list, the previous list, or whether the global handler is enabled.
origin.example:
options(progressr.handlers = NULL)
first <- make_progression_handler("rec", enable = TRUE, target = "file")
second <- make_progression_handler("other", enable = TRUE, target = "file")
handlers(rec = first)
cat(length(handlers()), " ", names(handlers()), "\n", sep = "")
previous <- handlers(extra = second, append = TRUE)
cat(length(previous), "\n", sep = "")
cat(length(handlers()), "\n", sep = "")

translation.description: Read or replace the progression handlers, and record whether the global handler is enabled.

arguments.name: handlers
arguments.text: Handlers, or one list or tuple of handlers. A string looks up handler_<name> and then <name> in the progressr package.

arguments.name: append
arguments.text: If True, concatenate onto the current list. The call returns the previous list.

arguments.name: on_missing
arguments.text: error, warning, or ignore when a named handler is missing. A unique prefix matches.

arguments.name: global_
arguments.text: R's global. True enables the flag, False disables it, and float('nan') queries it. global is a Python keyword.

translation.details: With no arguments, return the current list. If none was set, the default object is callable and, when invoked, raises an error whose text says handler_txtprogressbar is not translated. It does not draw a bar. A validator attribute that returns false drops the handler. Full global calling-handler registration is the flag global_ queries.
translation.value: The current list, the previous list, or whether the global handler is enabled.
translation.example:
from progressr.factory import make_progression_handler
from progressr.handlers import handlers
from progressr.options import set_option

set_option("progressr.handlers", None)
first = make_progression_handler("rec", enable=True, target="file")
second = make_progression_handler("other", enable=True, target="file")
handlers(rec=first)
current = handlers()
print(len(current), current._names[0])
previous = handlers(extra=second, append=True)
print(len(previous))
print(len(handlers()))
